HydroPin – digital twin viewer

The 3rd-phase prototype board (hardware list of 18 Nov 2026) as the twin sees it: move the valves, open a leak tap, read P1, P2 and F0, and replay five minutes of what the ESP32 would publish.

The prototype bench in 3D, built from the same geometry and twin as the simulation: turn it, change the valves, open a leak tap and watch the water.

A simulated early-morning irrigation shift (sectors 1 + 3) replayed minute by minute through the full chain: twin → virtual sensors → M1 + M2 → fusion → decision. A split lateral in block B12 (≈ 3 % of the flow) starts at minute 95.

    Prototype bench twin – set the valves, open a leak
    
   
   
    
    
    
    
    
   
    
   
    Angles: 0° = open, 82° = shut. Leaks are calibrated holes at the end of the tap tube (bench-twin recommendation). All values are EPANET results of the twin, solved in advance for every setting of the sliders.

      Pressure waves – slow motion
      
   
      
    
    
    
    
   
      
   
      
   
      
   
   
      Pick an event: the pipes turn red where the pressure rises and blue where it falls, at the speed of the wave (≈ 150 m/s in the PE pipes, 58 m/s in the soft hose), slowed down so the eye can follow. Computed by the transient solver at R1 = R2 = 65°, V1 = V2 = 78.0° without leak; the valve sliders above do not apply while a wave plays.
      
  
      
 
      
 
      
  
      What you are looking at
      
   
        
   
        Stripes in the pipes move at the real water speed from the twin (a few cm/s). Drops fall from the open tap and from the return pipe at a rate that follows their flow. The laptop shows what the dashboard would display.
